Medium Affected: WATER

CALLER IS REPORTING THAT A FAULTY DIESEL FUEL HOSE SPRAYED DIESEL FUEL ALL OVER THE GAS STATION. THE REPORTING PARTY STATED THAT THIS MORNING THEY PLACED THE HOSE IN THE TRUCK, SQUEEZED THE HANDLE, BUT NO FUEL CAME OUT. A COUPLE OF SECONDS LATER, DIESEL FUEL STARTED SHOOTING OUT OF THE SIDES OF THE HOSE. THE CALLER RAN INTO THE STORE TO ALERT THE MANAGER BUT HE STATED THAT HE WAS BUSY WITH THE DONUTS. THE REPORTING PARTY THEN RAN OUTSIDE AND HIT THE EMERGENCY SHUT OFF BUTTON. WHEN THEY WENT BACK IN TO INQUIRE ABOUT THE INCIDENT THE MANAGER STATED THAT SOMETHING LIKE THIS HAS OCCURRED BEFORE AND HE THINKS SOMEONE CUT THE HOSE. THE CALLER STATED THEY WATCHED THE DIESEL FUEL RUN INTO A DITCH THAT DRAINS DIRECTLY INTO THE CHESAPEAKE BAY.

properties.content:

Nearest City: LA
Incident Type: VESSEL
Material: SHELL TULLUS 46
Medium Affected: OTHER
Suspected Responsible Party: GOOD STREAK MARINE, INC
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 1 gallons
AT APPROXIMATELY 0815 HRS ON MARCH 8TH, A 1/4" HYDRAULIC CRANE HOSE BEGAN SPRAYING A THIN LINE OF HYDRAULIC OIL ON DECK. THE CRANE WAS SHUT DOWN AT FIRST SIGN OF LEAKAGE. APPROXIMATELY 1-2 GALLON OF PRODUCT WAS COLLECTED ON DECK, IMMEDIATELY CLEANED UP USING OIL ABSORBANT PADS, AND THE PADS WERE THEN DISPOSED OF PROPERLY. THE CAPTAIN, THIRD PARTY PERSONNEL, AND CREW MEMBERS IMMEDIATELY INSPECTED THE SURROUNDING WATER SURFACE AND FOUND NO SHEEN INDICATING THAT ANY PRODUCT HAD SPILLED INTO THE WATER. SINCE THERE WAS NO INDICATION OF A SHEEN AND NO OTHER SIGNS OF ANY TYPE OF SPILLAGE HAVING OCCURRED, THE INCIDENT WAS NOT REPORTED IN REFERENCE TO 40 CFR 110 GUIDELINES. THE INCIDENT WAS RECORDED IN THE VESSEL'S ROUGH LOG AND THE CUSTOMER LOG. APPROXIMATELY 24 HOURS LATER, IT WAS LEARNED THAT THE M/V GENESIS REPORTED RECEIVING A NEGLIGIBLE MIST ON THEIR WINDOW. DUE TO THIS OBSERVATION, WE ARE SUBMITTING A REPORT TO THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER.

Report Description
***THIS REPORT WAS RECEIVED VIA THE WEB REPORTING SYSTEM*** A CITIZEN CALLED THE LAKEWOOD POLICE DEPARTMENT TO REPORT OIL IN THE WATER RUNNING DOWN A CURB IN A RESIDENTIAL AREA. ON ARRIVAL, OFFICERS TRACED THE SOURCE OF THE OIL TO THE END OF A DRIVEWAY. OFFICERS CONTACTED A RESIDENT WHO INITIALLY ADMITTED TO WASHING OIL OFF HIS DRIVEWAY. WHEN CONFRONTED WITH THE FACT THAT THE AMOUNT OF OIL IN THE GUTTER WAS MORE THAN SIMPLY WHAT WOULD HAVE WASHED OFF A DRIVEWAY, THE RESPONSIBLE PARTY BECAME UNCOOPERATIVE AND DENIED INVOLVEMENT. FIRE DEPARTMENT PERSONNEL SUCCESSFULLY DAMMED THE RUNOFF, BUT NOT BEFORE SOME REACHED A STORM DRAIN. A MITIGATION COMPANY ARRIVED AND REMOVED THE REMAINING OIL AND RESIDUE FROM THE GUTTER. THE LOCAL WASTEWATER COMPANY WAS NOTIFIED OF THE DISCHARGE. THE AFFECTED STORM DRAIN DID NOT APPEAR TO EMPTY INTO A WATERWAY IN THE IMMEDIATE VICINITY. SUSPECT WAS CITED FOR ILLEGAL DUMPING.

SkyTruth Analysis

Report DescriptionNEEC INCIDENT NOTIFICATION: CAPSIZING OR RISK OF CAPSIZING POLLUTION FROM A VESSEL. 2023/03/04 09:49 AFTER ASSESSING CASE, NO POLLUTION WAS RELEASED FROM TUG PRIDE AND THERE IS NO ONGOING THREAT OF POLLUTION. CASE CLOSED FOR E.R. 2023/03/04 09:12 ADVISE THAT TUG PRIDE REPORTS SHE HAS BEEN RIGHTED AND THAT THERE IS NO SIGN OF POLLUTION. PHOTOS TO BE FORWARDED TO ER. MARINE OCCURENCE REPORT ATTACHED. 2023/03/04 08:36 ADVISES THAT, AFTER TAKING A CLOSER LOOK AT TUG PRIDE, IT DOES NOT APPEAR ITS HULL HAS SUFFERED ANY SIGNIFICANT DAMAGE. THE STARBOARD SIDE OF THE HULL IS SITTING ON WOODEN PILES AND FORECASTED WINDS AND WATER LEVELS WILL NOT BE STRONG OR HIGH ENOUGH TO FLOAT PRIDE OFF WITHOUT ANY ASSISTANCE. PICTURES ATTACHED. 2023/03/04 06:51 ADVISES THAT, AS NOTICED BY THEIR WATCHKEEPING TEAM AROUND 2 AM THIS MORNING, THE TUG PRIDE/CFN6705, MOORED JUST AHEAD OF THE GRIFFON, HAS HEELED OVER AS A RESULT OF THE HIGH WATER LEVELS AND GOT HUNG UP ON ITS SHORE MOORING ARRANGEMENTS. AS A RESULT ITS OUTER PORT SIDE HAS DIPPED BELOW THE SURFACE. AT THE TIME OF THE OBSERVATION, THERE WAS NO ONE ON BOARD AND IT DOES NOT APPEAR THAT PRIDE HAD BEGUN FLOODING INSIDE. DECK LIGHTS WERE STILL ON AND POLLUTION WAS OBSERVED AROUND THE TUG. THE GRIFFON TEAM CONTACTED THE FERRY ST. CLAIR 5 WHICH IN TURN CONTACTED THE TUG PRIDE"S CAPTAIN, WHO WAS 4 HOURS AWAY AT THAT TIME - IT IS UNKNOWN IF HE WAS ON HIS WAY WHEN THIS REPORT WAS RECEIVED.
